vignette: A 45-year-old man has progressive right-sided hearing loss and tinnitus, then numbness of the right face and, later, unsteadiness with a right-sided intention tremor. MRI shows a mass in the right cerebellopontine angle extending into the internal auditory canal.
stem: Which cerebellar structure accounts for the last symptoms?

options.text: Right flocculus and cerebellar hemisphere (lobule VI, Crus I)

explanation: A vestibular schwannoma compresses the eighth nerve first, then the trigeminal nerve, then the flocculus and the anterior cerebellar hemisphere beside the middle cerebellar peduncle, producing ipsilateral limb ataxia and gaze-evoked nystagmus; cerebellar signs are ipsilateral because the outflow crosses twice.
